The two variables are strongly correlated (r ≈ -0.55), so D is unlikely. On direction, I'm relying on physical reasoning and did not run a statistical direction test. Large-scale atmospheric circulation, which geopotential height represents, drives precipitation: high geopotential height means subsidence and suppressed precipitation, and low height means lifting and more precipitation. Precipitation does not plausibly drive the height field in the same way. That points to B.

ANSWER: B
